beats.text: You can now download a complete spatial physics world model directly to your own computer for zero dollars.

beats.text: Lightricks just open-weighted LTX-2.5, an advanced open foundation model designed for real-time video generation, camera control, and robotic physical simulation.
beats.show_cue: The official LTX-2.5 announcement post with sample physics simulation clips.

beats.text: Here is the simple version. Normal video models guess the next flat picture. A world model simulates physical laws in three dimensions, calculating how objects bounce, slide, and collide in real time.
beats.show_cue: A simulation video showing simulated object interactions and bouncing physics.

beats.text: The catch. You need twenty-four gigabytes of video memory to run inference smoothly, and aggressive camera pans can still soften fine geometric detail.
beats.show_cue: The hardware requirements table highlighting the 24GB VRAM recommendation.

beats.text: If you build in robotics, game development, or creative pipelines, grab the open weights. Open source AI just entered the physics engine business.
